title: How to Fix System Errors That Prevent Windows Shutdown? - GeeksforGeeks
content:
It can be very annoying to face technical issues while shutting down your Windows system. These issues can stem from various sources like software interference, faulty drivers, or damaged system files. The good news is that there are effective ways to troubleshoot and fix errors that prevent Windows from shutting down. In this guide, we will explain how to repair errors that prevent you from shutting down the system.

Table of Content

  • Quick Fixing Methods to Shutdown Computer
    • Method 1: Using Command Prompt
    • Method 2: Force Shut Down Your PC
    • Method 3: Run the Power Troubleshooter
    • Method 4: Kill Processes to Shut Down the Computer
    • Method 5: Using Run Dialog Box
  • Advanced Fixing Method to Shutdown Computer
    • Method 6: Run the SFC command
    • Method 7: Using Power Option Settings
    • Method 8: Create a Shutdown Shortcut Button
    • Method 9: Perform System Restore Point
    • Method 10: Manage your Startup Applications
    • Method 11: Upgrade Windows to its Latest version

Quick Fixing Methods to Shutdown Computer

First, try these quick-fix methods to shut down your computer. These methods are not only easy but require only a few steps to rectify the Windows shutdown issue.

Method 1: Using Command Prompt

Step 1: Open Command Prompt as an administrator.

Step 2: Type the following command and hit the Enter key.

Shutdown /p

Method 2: Force Shut Down Your PC

Try to force a shutdown of your PC if it troubles normal shutdown. To force the shutdown of the computer, press and hold the power button. If the PC is charging, turn off the power for five to ten minutes by disconnecting it from the electrical outlet.

Avoid attaching any transferring cables during this time. Then turn on your computer again and attempt a normal shutdown to see if the issue is resolved.

Method 3: Run the Power Troubleshooter

Step 1: Press the Windows key + R and type.

msdt.exe /id PowerDiagnostic

Step 2: Under Troubleshoot and help prevent computer problem dialog box. Click Next to proceed.

Step 3: Click the Close button after it resolves the shutdown issue

The troubleshooter will start detecting and diagnosing the issue. In our case, it's showing No changes or updates were necessary because my computer's power or shut down button is working fine. But if your system has any problem, it will troubleshoot that issue.

Method 4: Kill Processes to Shut Down the Computer

Step 1: Right-click on the taskbar and select Task Manager.

Step 2: Choose a process to be killed. Right-click on that process and select ‘End task.’

Step 3: Continue with all other open apps, excluding Windows Explorer.

Check if the issue is resolved or not. If not try these advanced troubleshooting methods to fix Fix System Errors That Prevent Windows Shutdown issues.

Method 5: Using Run Dialog Box

Step 1: Open Run by pressing the Window + R button.

Step 2: Type the following command then press Enter

shutdown /s /f /t 0

Advanced Fixing Method to Shutdown Computer

Method 6: Run the SFC command

Step 1: Open CMD and run it as administrator.

Step 2: Click on the Yes button to allow the system to make changes.

Step 3: Now, type 'sfc/scan' command.

This will repair all the corruption inside your Windows and repair those. Once it is done, restart your system and your issue will be fixed.

Method 7: Using Power Option Settings

Step 1: Open the Control Panel click the dropdown menu and select the Large Iconsand option

Step 2: Now Look for the Power Options settings, and click to open it.

Step 3: Select the "Choose what the power button does" option from the Power Options menu.

Step 4: Select the 'Change settings that are currently unavailable' option.

Step 5: Now look for the 'Turn on fast startup' option. Uncheck this option.

Step 6: After unchecking the fast startup option, click on the 'Save changes' button to apply the changes.

To check whether the problem has been fixed, try shutting down your computer once more. If still not solved, try this shortcut method

Method 8: Create a Shutdown Shortcut Button

we can create the shortcut key to shut down the PC. So how to create the shortcut key? Here are the steps to create a shortcut key to shut down your PC.

Step 1: Right-click on a space on your desktop click the 'New' option and choose 'Text Document'.

Step 2: You will see a new text document on your desktop. To open it, double-click on it.

Step 3: In the text document, type the following command

shutdown /s /t  0

Step 4: Click on "File" in the top menu, then select "Save As." Name the file "shutdown.bat" and choose "All Files" from the "Save as type" dropdown menu. Click "Save" to save the file.

Step 5: Select the newly formed shutdown with a right-click. Select the Create shortcut option.

Step 6: You will find a new shortcut icon on the desktop. Right-click on this icon and click the 'Properties' context menu.

Step 7: Select the 'Change Icon' button under the 'Shortcut' tab of the Properties box.

Step 8: Select an icon from the list of alternatives or search for an icon file of your own to use as your shortcut.

Step 9: Click OK to apply the changes, then click Apply and OK again to close the Properties window.

You need to just double-click on that and your system is going to automatically shut down. If this is not fixing your problem, there is some issue with your Windows.

Method 9: Perform System Restore Point

Step 1: Open the search box, type 'Restore,' and Click on Create a restore point to open it.

Step 2: Click Next under Restore system files and settings.

Step 3: Select System Restore from the System Protection menu.

Step 4: Click Next after choosing your restore point.

This allows you to restore your system to a prior state. If this method doesn't work then go for the next other method.

Method 10: Manage your Startup Applications

Sometimes startup applications can prevent PCs from shutting down. There comes a need to disable these startup applications to check if the PC shutting down properly or not. Here’s how you can disable startup applications on your computer.

Step 1: Open Settings, select Apps, and then click Startup.

Step 2: Toggle off all the apps or programs and check if your computer is shutting down properly or not.

If none of the above methods work, then you must update your Windows version. Try the last method to resolve your Windows shutdown issue.

Method 11: Upgrade Windows to its Latest version

Update Windows to the most recent version to fix any bugs and speed up your computer performance. Check for Windows updates Windows if any and update it ASAP. If you are using Windows 10, Then It's time to update it. So update Windows 10 to Windows 11 now!

Conclusion

System errors hindering the shutdown process of Windows must be fixed in order to keep your system functional. As stated above, you can put your shutdown troubles to rest by learning and applying the right techniques. Timely updates, antivirus scans, and regular system maintenance ensure that the systems will not suffer such errors again. If that does not solve the issues, it might be a good idea to turn to experts in order to keep your system perfect.
